findings.message: The guard decides whether the verify verdict is for HEAD by comparing commit dates with the verdict's `at` time (`git rev-list -1 --since="$at" HEAD`). It never records or compares which commit was verified. Any commit that reaches HEAD with an older committer date passes as verified, for example a fast-forward pull or a `git reset --hard` / checkout to another commit. Fix: record the verified HEAD sha (and a clean or dirty flag) in phases.verify, and hold when it differs from `git rev-parse HEAD`. Keep the dirty check. Add a variant test covering a commit after verify, a fast-forward to an older-dated commit, and a reset to another commit.
findings.scenario: A teammate commits Y (committer date 09:30) on top of X. You run /specclaw:verify on X at 10:00 (PASS, at=10:00). At 10:05 you run `git pull --ff-only`, so HEAD = Y. `rev-list --since=10:00 HEAD` is empty and the tree is clean, so the guard exits 0. The PASS for X is accepted for unverified code Y.

findings.message: The fallback order (git.base_branch, else origin/HEAD with `origin/` stripped, else main) is written twice: once in branch.ts (`configured || remote || 'main'`) and once in lib/base-ref.sh base_merge_base. The shared fixture covers only the config parsing, not this fallback chain. The two copies agree today, but nothing tests them against each other. Drive both from one table, or note the pairing in both files.

base-ref.sh accepts a `git.base_branch` written as a remote ref, such as `origin/main`: it tries `origin/origin/main`, then `origin/main`, which resolves. branch.ts compares that value literally with `git branch --show-current` (`main`), so the branch guard never fires for that spelling. The size cap and the done guard do work with it. Strip a leading `origin/` in branch.ts as well, or reject the spelling in both readers.

`git merge-base` exits 1 when there is no common ancestor, but it also fails for other reasons (a corrupt object, a timeout). Every failure is mapped to `-`, which is then reported as 'no merge-base (a shallow clone?)'. The outcome is still conservative: size exits 2, and the done guard checks every change. Only the stated cause can be wrong. Treat exit 1 as `-` and surface any other exit as a git failure.

The template comment says the default test list is `SIZE_EXCLUDE in bin/specclaw-verify`. The CamelCase patterns live in a second array, `SIZE_EXCLUDE_CASED`. references/full/verify.md names both arrays; the template should too.

Every Edit, Write and NotebookEdit in a specclaw project now runs up to three git subprocesses (each with a 3s timeout) and reads config.yaml before the gate decides. This happens even in `warn` mode, and even when the target is under `.specclaw/`, which is exempt anyway. Consider skipping the branch lookup when the target is already exempt.
